summary: R2-2 (termination bound) and R2-5 (putIfAbsent for first acquisition) are genuinely fixed and consistent between SPEC and backlog. R2-1 and R2-3 are fixed in the prose but NOT in the tables that drive the build: the superseded 'O(1) pages via startAfter' discovery survives verbatim in backlog M4.8, in the SPEC's test-plan row, in the SPEC's own Tasks table and in Cost impact, where it now flatly contradicts AC5's zero-LIST bound. The new lease-carried cursor also introduces two things the spec does not settle: who writes lastCheckpoint and at what cadence (its 'costs no extra request' claim is false in one branch), and an absent/unreadable-lease fallback that the spec calls 'confined to cold start' although M4's own voluntary release can produce it with a full chain present -- and AC5 exempts exactly that path from the only assertion that would catch it.
verified_fixed: R2-2: the renew-interval bound is arithmetically right (TTL 30s, renew at TTL/3 = 10s, commitBatchInterval 250ms => ~40 commits), strictly weaker-than-safe compared with in-flight depth, consistent with 03-metadata-and-cas.md section 7's 'bounded number of further attempts', and SPEC:384-390 and backlog M4.6 now say the same thing including the explicit warning against capping at in-flight depth.

R2-5: scope item 2 (SPEC:117-122) matches binstore-spi/src/main/java/binjava/binstore/BinStore.java:60-73 exactly -- putIfMatch on an ABSENT key throws and is deliberately not folded into the lost-race empty Optional. AC2 is consistent with both paths (unheld lease => putIfAbsent losers get empty Optional; expired lease => putIfMatch losers get empty Optional). Backlog M4.3 carries the correction.
R2-1(a): the lease read at recovery is not assumed -- 03-metadata-and-cas.md:163-165 has a reader looking up ctl/lease/<slot>.json to learn (holderPodId, epoch) before it can follow the chain at all.
R2-1(c): zero LIST is achievable for a tier-3 consumer that holds no lease -- it needs a plain GET of the lease object, not a CAS, so no lease of its own is required.

Minors: AC9's saturation clause is present (SPEC:429-435); 'single-NODE deployment' at SPEC:205 is accurate under S=1; the stale-citation list names .agents/skills/spec/SKILL.md:40 and that line really does read 'invariants I1-I4' (verified); the 16 backlog rows M4.0-M4.15 are 1:1 with the SPEC's 16-row Tasks table.

findings.title: R2-1's fix reached the prose and AC5, not the four places that decide what gets built; the superseded page bound survives and now contradicts AC5
findings.failure_scenario: backlog.md:223 (M4.8) still reads 'Newest-checkpoint discovery must be O(1) pages via `startAfter`, not a scan of a prefix that grows with uptime' and never mentions the lease-carried lastCheckpoint cursor. SPEC.md:457's test-plan row still reads 'Newest-checkpoint discovery is O(1) pages with >=50 checkpoints present | a discovery that pages the whole ckpt/ prefix' -- the exact bound round 2 demonstrated is satisfied by the naive list-and-take-last, because 50 checkpoints fit in one 1,000-key page. SPEC.md:501 (Tasks M4.8) still says 'O(1)-page newest-checkpoint discovery'. SPEC.md:370-372 (Cost impact) still says 'Recovery is the one place a LIST is permitted (R2) ... the discovery path above keeps it O(1) pages', which directly contradicts AC5 at :400-408 ('no `list` at all'). Concretely: whoever implements M4.8 works from the backlog row and the test-plan row -- those are the artifacts the task and the TDD cycle consume -- writes list(ckpt/ prefix) and takes the last key, writes the T1 test the test-plan row specifies with 50 checkpoints, gets a red then a green, and lands. Nothing fails. The design paragraph that says the cursor comes from the lease is prose in a section M4.8's implementer has no reason to re-read. Recovery then issues one LIST per node per recovery on M5's tier-3 fallback ladder at up to 300 plugin nodes, against cost.md R15's ~1 LIST/s ceiling -- the precise cost bug this spec's own :292-295 says would surface two milestones later. Note also that `startAfter` in the backlog row is itself circular in the way round 2 named: startAfter needs a cursor, and the row names no source for it.
findings.remedy: Rewrite backlog M4.8's discovery sentence to the lease-cursor mechanism (or to the bound only -- see the process note), replace the SPEC test-plan row's bound with 'issues zero list calls' and a mutation column naming list-and-take-last, fix SPEC Tasks M4.8, and rewrite Cost impact :370-372 so it does not assert a LIST the acceptance criterion forbids.

findings.title: The lease cursor's writer and cadence are unspecified, and the two readings of one sentence disagree on cost and on staleness
findings.failure_scenario: SPEC:277-278 says the lease 'is already rewritten on every renew' (hence 'costs nothing') and in the same breath that lastCheckpoint is 'updated by the leaseholder when it writes a checkpoint'. Those are different cadences: renew is TTL/3 (~10 s), checkpoints are every K deltas or T seconds (corpus defaults K=1,000, T=60). An implementer at M4.3/M4.8 must pick, and the spec neither picks nor states the consequence of either pick. (a) Update at checkpoint time: that is a second putIfMatch against the lease per checkpoint, so 'costs no extra request' is false and Cost impact :366-368's 'Checkpoints cost one PUT per K deltas or T seconds' is off by a factor of two; worse, the leaseholder now has two independent writers of the one CAS object whose lost race the spec elsewhere defines as the fencing signal (test-plan row :452, 'Renewal failure stops sequencing immediately' -- and the SPI returns the same empty Optional for 'my own checkpoint write moved the version' as for 'I was fenced'), so a self-inflicted race between the renew timer and the checkpoint writer is indistinguishable from a takeover and the obvious reading of the spec's own rule stops the cluster's only sequencer. (b) Update at renew time: cost claim holds and there is one writer, but the pointer is then up to one renew interval stale, and AC5's 'at most K delta GETs' silently becomes 'at most 2K' -- a request-count assertion written to the literal criterion would fail against a correct implementation.
findings.remedy: Say which write carries the pointer and make it the only writer of the lease object, then state the resulting staleness bound and make AC5's delta-GET bound match it.

findings.title: 'Confined to cold start' is not true, and AC5 exempts from testing the only path in the design that can issue an unbounded LIST
findings.failure_scenario: SPEC:287-290: 'an absent or unreadable lease falls back to the paged scan, which is correct but O(n) -- so it is confined to cold start, where there is no chain to scan yet.' Two reachable states inside M4 falsify that. (1) Voluntary release ships in M4 (Out-list: 'the mechanism it uses -- voluntary release -- ships here'; backlog M4.3 'acquire/renew/release') and nothing says whether release deletes the lease object or rewrites it as expired. If it deletes -- which is also what makes scope item 2's putIfAbsent path reachable outside cold start -- then between release and the next acquisition the lease is ABSENT while a 5,000-delta chain exists, and every recovering process and tier-3 consumer that reads in that window takes the O(n) paged scan. At M5's 300-node tier-3 fan-out that is a LIST storm on the one path cost.md R15 caps at ~1 LIST/s. (2) A takeover rewrites the lease with (holder, epoch+1); nothing says the new holder must carry the previous holder's lastCheckpoint forward, so a dropped field leaves a present lease with an absent pointer and a long chain -- a case the spec's two 'degenerate cases' do not cover at all. Then AC5:409-410 exempts 'the cold-start fallback path (no lease object)' from the zero-LIST assertion, so the only path in the whole design that can issue an unbounded LIST is precisely the one no criterion constrains, and the mislabelling as cold start is what makes that exemption look safe.
findings.remedy: Specify that release and acquisition preserve the lease object and its lastCheckpoint (a tombstone with an expired deadline rather than a delete), and either bound the absent-lease fallback with a criterion or state plainly that an absent lease is an operator-visible degraded state rather than a normal one.

findings.title: R2-3's and R2-5's fixes reached the backlog and the prose but not the SPEC's own Tasks table or test plan, so the spec contradicts the authoritative task list
findings.failure_scenario: SPEC Tasks :496 still reads 'M4.3 | Lease record and key grammar; `putIfMatch` acquire/renew/release', contradicting the spec's own scope item 2 at :117-122 and backlog M4.3; the Design summary at :188 likewise still reads 'putIfMatch for the lease'. SPEC Tasks :498 still reads 'M4.5 | ... golden files for both shapes' with no mention of CONTINUE, while backlog M4.5 correctly says 'golden files for EVERY shape -- v0, SEAL and CONTINUE'; no scope item and no acceptance criterion mentions CONTINUE either, so inside the SPEC it is still demanded by a test-plan row (:455) and owned only by a Design paragraph. Test-plan row :461 lacks AC9's new saturation clause ('PUT count unchanged from 1 pod to 6'), which is the wording the AC minor was raised about. Test-plan row :451 has no case that fails first against putIfMatch on an absent key, so the R2-5 defect has no falsifying test. Failure: a reader of M4.15's VERIFIED.md or the milestone review checks the milestone against the SPEC's Tasks table and test plan, which disagree with the backlog on three rows; whichever the implementer happens to read decides what ships.
findings.remedy: Update the SPEC's Tasks table and test plan to match the scope items and the backlog rows, and add a test-plan row whose mutation is putIfMatch-on-an-absent-key.

findings.title: The stale-I1-I4 enumeration is incomplete and nothing owns the citations it leaves stale
findings.failure_scenario: .agents/skills/review/SKILL.md:93 reads 'Does a claimed invariant (I1-I4) actually hold under the failure it names?' and is not in the spec's list of stale citations -- yet it is the brief handed to the reviewer of every M4 commit, so the reviewers of M4.11 and M4.13 are prompted with a four-invariant list and will not ask about I5, the one the corpus singles out as the invariant a plausible implementation violates by accident. Beyond that, the spec names four stale citations, corrects one (roadmap), exempts one on principle (ADR-0002), and leaves two research documents plus spec/SKILL.md:40 stale with no backlog row -- so the correction exists only in this paragraph and the next spec author still copies I1-I4 from the worked example.
findings.remedy: Add the review skill to the list, and add one backlog row owning the remaining stale citations rather than leaving them named-but-unowned.

process_note: The round-3 call was right, and the reason is narrower than 'a wrong spec is expensive'. At round 2 rule 10 forbade landing (majors block on changes-requested), rule 12's 'split it' remedy does not apply to a single new document whose defect is in its argument rather than its size, and arguing correct findings would have been false -- so fixing was the only honest move, and sdd.md rules 7 and 8 point the same way. But this round again found its defects in the previous round's fix rather than in the original change, which is exactly the pattern rule 12 was written from, and the cause is visible: the SPEC specifies a mechanism it did not have to specify. The third option nobody took was to SHRINK rather than split -- keep AC5 ('recovery issues zero list calls'), state the constraint, and let M4.8's own commit choose the mechanism under an ADR if it needs one. sdd.md rule 6 asks a spec for checkable criteria, not for implementations. That shape is also the cheapest fix for this round: deleting the discovery mechanism from the SPEC and the backlog row resolves R3-1, R3-2 and R3-3 at once, because all three are defects in a mechanism the spec need not contain. Recommend round 4 does that rather than adding a fourth layer of prose about the lease pointer.
implementability: Not yet. M4.1-M4.15 cannot be worked end to end without inventing two decisions the spec does not make: which write carries lastCheckpoint and at what cadence (R3-2, needed at M4.3 and M4.8), and whether release and takeover preserve the lease object and its pointer (R3-3, needed at M4.3). Everything else -- the seal's two branches, idempotency, the ack rule, the observable's shape, the SEAL/CONTINUE ADR being left as 'either variant or separate object type' -- is either decided or explicitly delegated to a task's own ADR, which is fine.
